review: Request: at round 15 Moss (6.9 roots in item-2-moss-11, health 100, energy 40, no tool, support or measuring equipment owned) asked for a physically grounded way to expose the interior of a small owned root sample and measure its actual moisture change against an equal untreated reference, with feasible preparation, support and measurement methods identified, nothing granted, enough roots kept for meals and no automatic preservation, safety or reward. World Agent decision: develop (learning 4) a general operation to prepare and compare material samples with mode start|prepare|measure|tend|stop, sourceItemId, sampleQuantity, preparation split|slice, toolId, supportId, measurementDeviceId, location, durationRounds and trialId: start 1 round and 0.2 energy, allocating a default 0.1 sample and an equal reference from one owned stack with inherited state and never the whole supply; prepare 1 round and 0.5 energy per attempted split or slice with an acquired tool whose geometry, edge, strength and cleanliness are represented, on a support validated as in air-dry-food-trial; measure 1 round and 0.2 energy per sample on a real calibrated device, implementing a general measuring mechanism with paid construction and calibration if none exists, recording calibration, resolution, uncertainty, tare, time, ids and readings, reporting mass change as mass change and a loss below resolution as unresolved, not zero, and disclosing no absolute moisture; tend 1 round and 0.2 energy; stop 1 round and no energy, releasing the reference once and leaving pieces and support for real pickup; drying only through genuinely exposed surfaces by a bounded transfer with surface area, accessible water, temperature, humidity, airflow, rain and latent heat, conserving dry matter and solutes, while whole food keeps the existing no-evaporation rule; evidence only for experience, and no preservation, safety, nutrition or reward. Registry check: no long-ex21 interface weighs or compares masses; ex19 lever-mass-comparator@1 is that general mechanism but is scoped to long-ex19 and cannot be installed here. Implemented, as two packages installed in this order. beam-mass-comparator@1 (ability beam-mass-comparator, handler long.beam-mass-comparator, events beam-comparator-*, learning 4 with 0.5 study energy per round) is the ex19 comparator built by its own factory under a new identity and equivalence, with the same geometry, torque and stiction physics, costs, texts and rules: assess; three paid assembly rounds of 0.5 with an own branch beam, a stone or flint fulcrum piece or outcrop and an own non-food, non-decaying reference piece of at most 1 unit; test readings of 0.2 each until three empty and three loaded readings from both directions repeat and close; rain voids a test; inspect and dismantle. compare-material-samples@1 (ability compare-material-samples, handler long.compare-material-samples, learning 4, no study energy) is the one ability assigned to Moss. start (sourceItemId, sampleQuantity 0.1 to 1 in tenths with default 0.1 and larger amounts only by the explicit argument, durationRounds default 10) checks the source with the ex19 whole-food rule, pays 0.2 through workPay and separates the sample and an equal reference with workReserve; both stay whole, carried and reserved with their tenths, decay, harvest time, origin and the food water record (root 0.75, berry 0.85 water, the representation's assumption); the stack must keep at least 0.1 unreserved, so Moss's default leaves 6.7 of 6.9; the split is the world's existing tenths accounting, so no cut is made and no surface is exposed. prepare (preparation, toolId, supportId, location) pays 0.5 and cuts the sample with the person's carried whole stone or flint unit that passes the ex19 thin-slice edge rule (contact-resistance index at least 8 and not below the food's, edge radius at most 0.0002, controlled contact, not fractured or contaminated), then lays the pieces cut face up at location in reach on the person's own support that passes the air-dry-food-trial support rule (non-food, non-toxic, non-perishable, dry, rigid, unfractured, clean, one whole unit per 0.04 of covered ground) on firm, unobstructed, unoccupied ground, or at the centre of an existing food surface in reach that is not another person's; the support units are held in the trial record under the pieces; the edge keeps its contact record and gains no wear; the sample stack gains a visible geometry record and the representation's irreversible opened state with opening damage 1.1, but no representation surface, so its thin-layer rule never also moves this water. measure (measurementDeviceId) weighs the sample and the reference on the person's own tested beam-mass-comparator in reach, paying 0.2 per item: each item is seated and the reference slid in from both ends until the beam tips, giving its mass as a fraction of the reference piece at 0.02 half-beam resolution against the tested empty null range as tare, recorded with the calibration test readings and time, resolution, uncertainty, tip positions and trial and item ids; each item's first weighing stays its baseline, and later weighings give after/before mass-change and ratio intervals for each item and a reference-adjusted ratio carrying all four readings, reported as a decrease or increase only when the interval excludes 1 and otherwise as unresolved, below the resolution and not zero; weighing moves nothing and never shows water content. tend (location optional) pays 0.2 and turns the pieces in place, which changes no represented state, or moves an own support item with the pieces to a new checked point in reach; an existing surface cannot be moved. stop pays nothing. Every round an environmental process, not work, runs for every lying piece stack this operation has cut, whether or not its trial is open: evaporation = h/1200 x exposed cut-face area x (saturation vapour density at the face temperature - air humidity x saturation density at the air temperature) x 1080 s, with h = 10 x (1 + 0.5 x wind index) W/(m2 K) and the face temperature solving C (T - T0) = h A (T_air - T) dt - L x evaporation, with C from the pieces' water (4180 J/(kg K)) and dry matter (1500) and L = 2.45 MJ/kg, by 60 fixed bisection steps; evaporation is bounded by the free water above the representation's humidity equilibrium (0.1 + 0.25 x humidity of total mass) held within sqrt(1e-10 m2/s x 1080 s), about 0.33 mm, under the exposed faces; faces colder than the dew point gain condensate; rain on the pieces' footprint adds 0.01 x rain x area (the representation's coefficient), less under open refuges and none indoors, where wind is also zero; dry matter, quantity, nutrition and toxicity never change; the water goes to the general food water ledger and a hidden audit ledger keeps evaporation, condensation, rain, latent heat, heat from the air and the pieces' own heat; carried and whole food exchange nothing; ordinary decay continues at the representation's rate for opened food. The exposure window counts durationRounds from the cut; when it ends the trial completes with the comparison of the weighings, or ends indeterminate without a before and after weighing of the sample; spoilage of the sample ends it as failed, and anyone taking the pieces under the ordinary rules, stop or death end it as interrupted; every ending releases the reserved reference once (dropped at the death position on death), returns the support item to the site as an unowned stack and leaves the pieces lying, still exchanging water and ageing; nothing is refunded. Events: sample-trial-allocated, -cut, -placed, -weighed, -tended, -exchange (a simulation event with no amounts), -rained-on, -reduced, -removed, -spoiled, -reference-spoiled, -compared, -indeterminate, -stopped and -interrupted, with view metadata (ground-stack component, revision, trial, sample, reference, tool, support, instrument, position, footprint, form and pieces, start and update rounds, exposure progress, visible shrinkage or wetness, state pending, active, completed, indeterminate, failed or interrupted, preservation unverified, no badge, evidence event ids); visualComponents is empty; no satisfaction source, reward or practice milestone is added and the weighing event carries no qualified flag, so experience gets evidence only. Modeling assumptions: mass units are kg; the uncut sample is one compact skin-covered sphere of 1000 kg/m3 tissue, the ex17 food shape; split cuts it through the centre into two halves and slice into equal slabs no thicker than 5 mm, an assumed even hand-held stone-edge cut; each piece lies with one new cut face up and its larger face down, so the exposed area is one face per piece and the footprint the larger faces, never less than the inherited 0.04 per unit; skin and faces on the support exchange no water or heat; the exposed area does not shrink as pieces dry; the cut removes no mass and leaves no crumb, offcut or sap residue and, under the existing contact law, no edge wear, so a cut with a qualifying edge always succeeds and unsuitable tools are refused before any charge; turning has no represented consequence in this lumped model; free water evaporates as from a wet surface and no vapour sorption below the equilibrium is represented; no sunlight or radiation, rain heat, support conduction or soil-food water transfer is represented; all rain on the footprint is taken up, so there is no runoff; pieces start at the air temperature when laid or laid again; the comparator's passed validity test is its calibration, and readings are relative to its reference piece, not grams; weighing moves no water; base pickup, eat and drop take whole units, so pieces or reference portions under one unit cannot be moved or eaten with them afterwards and remain conserved stacks that age; an uncut trial waits without a window until it is prepared or stopped. Reuse: ex19 lever-mass-comparator@1 became the factory leverMassComparatorKit in long-ex19-lever-mass-comparison.ts, which builds LONG_EX19_LEVER_MASS_COMPARATOR with byte-identical JSON (sha256 checked in the test), the same handler, events and behaviour (all ex19 tests pass) and also the ex21 package, and offers read-only calibrated and weigh functions over the same physics; the ex19 thin-slice edge rule and the ex21 air-dry support rule, footprint and shrinkage classes are exported unchanged, and the JSON of their packages is hash-checked too; also reused are airExposureUnsupported and airExposureTrack, ex19MaterialWhole, HEAT from the ex17 thermal module, the food water API, scratchPhysical, the collective-work escrow and paid-work helpers and openRemember, while probe, navigate, gather, pickup and drop stay separate actions. What Moss can do now: Moss owns no stone or flint, support or device, so prepare and measure are refused with explicit missing prerequisites; after four rounds of study Moss can start a trial at once; cutting and laying need two stones from the start-2-stone outcrop about 4.8 away, and any gathered stone qualifies as edge and support; weighing needs beam-mass-comparator learned separately (4 rounds, 2 energy), a branch from canopy-69 about 0.6 away, a reference piece, three assembly rounds and six test readings; a throwaway check on the archived round-15 world ran this sequence for about 15 energy over about 50 rounds apart from walking, and showed a 0.1 root sample losing about 4 g of its 30 g of water in 24 rounds while every weighing against a 2 kg stone reference stayed between 0 and 0.114 of it, unresolved, and the rain that starts near round 48 voided the comparator test once. First release: no; the specification is self-consistent and implementable, so this is a real mechanism with real costs, state changes and events, whose honest present result for Moss's default sample is a mass change below the comparator's resolution.
